Dataset created adapted from the methodology followed by: Life Cycle Inventories and Life Cycle Assessments of Photovoltaic Systems 2020 Task 12 PV Sustainability, December 2020, DOI: 10.13140/RG.2.2.17977.19041

The lifetime of PV systems is estimated at 30 years based on the PEFCR PV electricity.

Technology:  Electricity production with grid-connected photovoltaic power plants.
Time period:  Time of publications

Extrapolations:  Use of PV technology data investigated for other countries (Switzerland). Correction of average yield with Swiss data.
Uncertainty:  None
Author: Romain Sacchi, PSI, romain.sacchi@psi.ch
PoR compatibility snapshot of the existing Morocco commercial PV recipe, migrated to ecoinvent 3.12. The medium-voltage output is a lossless plant interface to the original low-voltage-labelled recipe: no unreported transformer, losses, distribution service or grid generation is added. The source proxy technology shares, lifetime, cleaning quantities and manufacturing/construction supplier geographies are preserved. Country PVOUT retrieval date was not recorded in the source workbook. The source cleaning quantities are retained as supplied; they are not recomputed from module area or Morocco yield. The source calls this an OECD proxy, but its formulas weight all 33 report countries, including some countries outside the OECD.

datasets.comment:
The reference flow for the life cycle inventory is 1 square metre of wafer surface. The multi-crystalline silicon ingots are sawn into square wafers with a size 156.75x156.75 mm2 (0.0246 m2), a thickness of 180 um and a weight of 419 g/m2. The sawing losses are 120 um (95 um kerf loss and 25 um additional losses such as pot scrap, ingot top, squaring, cropping etc.) or 280 g/m2. The diamond wire is modelled as a stainless steel wire because data on industrial diamond manufacture are missing. Water is used as a cutting fluid.
Diamond sawing and cleaning of wafers. The process data include electricity use, water and working material consumption. Production wastes to be treated and process-specific waterborne pollutants are considered. No data on other process specific air emissions.
Location:  Data for RER, extrapolated to Chinese production.
Technology:  Use of diamond wire saws.
Time period:  Collection of data in 2005. Use of some data from older publications. Silicon demand, electricity consumption as well as diamond wire and water demand updated for 2018.
Production volume:  Approximately 105000 MW for total c-Si in 2018
Sampling:  Data collection by factory representatives. Environmental report and LCA studies. 
Extrapolations:  Extrapolation of European LCI data by changing the electricity mix.

Production of photovoltaic cells (156.75x156.75 mm2). Some inputs and emissions aggregated to protect sensitive data.
Cleaning, damage etching, texture etching, covering of backside, phosphor dotation, phosphor glass etching, printing of contacts, cleaning and quality testing.
Location:  Data of production in Europe, extrapolated to Chinese production.
Technology:  Average production technology of photovoltaic cells from wafers.
Time period:  Data investigated in 2004. Demand of electricity and metallisation paste updated for 2018.
Production volume:  Approximately 105000 MW for total c-Si in 2018
Sampling:  Data collected from 5 specific processes and companies (4 multi-Si + 1 single-Si processing company).
Extrapolations:  Data 2005 calculated from data 2004 by multiplying amounts of materials by solar cell area factor of 156*156/(125*125) = 1.56; energy scaled linearly with cell side length. Extrapolation of European LCI inventory data by adjusting the electricity mix.
Uncertainty:  None

Sampling:  Environmental reports, direct contacts with factory representatives and publication of plant data.

Uncertainty:  None

datasets.comment:
The reference flow for the life cycle inventory is 1 square metre of wafer surface. The single-crystalline silicon ingots are sawn into square wafers with a size 156.75x156.75 mm2 (0.0244 m2), a thickness of 170 um and a weight of 396 g/m2. The sawing losses are 121 um (95 um kerf loss and 26 um additional losses such as pot scrap, ingot top, squaring, cropping etc.) or 282 g/m2. The diamond wire is modelled as a stainless steel wire because data on industrial diamond manufacture are missing. Water is used as a cutting fluid.
Diamond sawing and cleaning of wafers. The process data include electricity use, water and working material consumption. Production wastes to be treated and process-specific waterborne pollutants are considered. No data on other process specific air emissions.
Location:  Data for RER, extrapolated to Chinese production.
Technology:  Use of diamond wire saws.
Time period:  Collection of data in 2005. Use of some data from older publications. Silicon demand, electricity consumption as well as diamond wire and water demand updated for 2018.
Production volume:  Approximately 105000 MW for total c-Si in 2018
Sampling:  Data collection by factory representatives. Environmental report and LCA studies. 
Extrapolations:  Extrapolation of European LCI data by changing the electricity mix.
Uncertainty:  None

datasets.comment:
This dataset represents a weighted average of the recycling efforts of four recycling facilities in Europe. The average transport distance of waste c-Si PV panels is assumed to be 500 km. The treatment of c-Si PV modules yields glass cullets, aluminium scrap and copper scrap, which are considered as co-products. The efforts of PV module takeback and recycling are economically allocated to the treatment and the recovered materials.
This dataset includes the transport of used crystalline silicon photovoltaic modules to the recycling facility as well as their dismantling and recycling. The consumption of energy and the disposal of waste material are also included. The takeback and recycling of the electric installation and the mounting structure are not included.
Location:  Europe
Technology:  Industry data.
Time period:  Time of publications.
Sampling:  Literature data.
Extrapolations:  Some generic datasets from ecoinvent have been used.
Uncertainty:  none
